issue_context.title: [10.0-preview.1] CS1591 warnings-as-errors caused by Program class being exposed as public
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

I'm in the middle of working on updating Swashbuckle.AspNetCore to support ASP.NET Core 10 and Microsoft.OpenApi v2 and stumbled into a compilation issue caused by [this new feature](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/preview/preview1/aspnetcore.md#improvements-to-integration-testing-of-apps-with-top-level-statements).

We have a test project where warnings-as-errors is enabled as part of testing XML documentation support, and when targeting `net10.0` the project fails to compile with the following error:

```text
Missing XML comment for publicly visible type or member 'Program'
```

This is extra puzzling, as the `Program.cs` file [already has code to manually expose the class](https://github.com/domaindrivendev/Swashbuckle.AspNetCore/blob/446c522d496363fec3d4c759546f7ae2a7fe318c/test/WebSites/WebApi/Program.cs#L37-L45):

```csharp
namespace WebApi
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Expose the Program class for use with <c>WebApplicationFactory</c>
    /// </summary>
    public partial class Program
    {
    }
}
```

I guess the easiest way to resolve this would be to have the source generator emit a `#pragma` to silence the documentation warnings.


### Expected Behavior

The project compiles with no warnings/errors.

### Steps To Reproduce

Build the `WebApi` project from https://github.com/domaindrivendev/Swashbuckle.AspNetCore/commit/446c522d496363fec3d4c759546f7ae2a7fe318c without [this workaround](https://github.com/domaindrivendev/Swashbuckle.AspNetCore/blob/446c522d496363fec3d4c759546f7ae2a7fe318c/test/WebSites/WebApi/WebApi.csproj#L11-L14).

### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

10.0.100-preview.1.25120.13

### Anything else?

_No response_

I have just cloned this to my machine to have a mess around.

> This is extra puzzling, as the `Program.cs` file [already has code to manually expose the class](https://github.com/domaindrivendev/Swashbuckle.AspNetCore/blob/446c522d496363fec3d4c759546f7ae2a7fe318c/test/WebSites/WebApi/Program.cs#L37-L45):

I am not sure if you noticed this but it successfully builds without your workaround if you take the partial class declaration and XML doc comment outside of the namespace.

Furthermore the analyzer warning ASP0027 does not display whilst the declaration is within a namespace.

At the point the declaration is not within a namespace the warning is shown, reintroducing this bug on removal.

When I have had to declare this in my own projects I have never done so within a namespace. It's almost like the implementation for this feature is ignoring the declaration when it is in a namespace hence you seeing this bug.

review_comments:
I _don't_ think this is right here. AFAIK, analyzers shouldn't trigger on generated code.

In the past, I've noticed that the `// <auto-generated />` marker on the file isn't sufficient. We might also want to emit `[GeneratedCode]` here to mark this type as generated.

You can see how we do it for [the OpenAPI XML generator](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/aa5687c0aa7a2600b5652da4cec2cbfba9e83314/src/OpenApi/gen/XmlCommentGenerator.Emitter.cs) and [the minimal API source generator](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/aa5687c0aa7a2600b5652da4cec2cbfba9e83314/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator/StaticRouteHandlerModel/StaticRouteHandlerModel.Emitter.cs).

This is not an analyzer, it's a compile warning. There were discussions in dotnet/roslyn to special case that specific one for generated code, but I'm not sure if anything was done yet, or if any decision was taken.

Projects that have `<GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>` in the .csproj will have the CS1591 compiler warning when the current generated code is output preventing building the solution

CS1591 looks as follows in this case
`Missing XML comment for publicly visible type or member 'Program'`

This `#pragma` should suppress this warning

Something important to note is that the project in the issue only has the CS1591 warning preventing the build due to them also having
`<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>`
That being said we still don't want this warning to flag for the generated code when the below option is stated in the project
`<GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>`
